starting-off.speaker: Awusah the Mayor
starting-off.text: Many salutations to you. What brings you to our little town?

options.text: I am an adventurer in search of quests.

steps.player: I am an adventurer in search of quests.

steps.speaker: Awusah the Mayor
steps.text: Hmm, well that could be quite fortuitous. We really could do with some help here. Our town seems to have come under a curse, and we are desperate to get it removed.

steps.player: A curse? What sort of curse?

steps.speaker: Awusah the Mayor
steps.text: Well first of all our fountain, which has served us for many years, suddenly dried up. We then started transporting water from the river, but what we carried would always have completely dried up by the time we

steps.speaker: Awusah the Mayor
steps.text: got it back to the village.

options.text: So what do you do for water now?

steps.player: So what do you do for water now?

steps.speaker: Awusah the Mayor
steps.text: Well it's tough. There is a guy who calls himself Ali the carter down in the market. He's from Pollnivneach, so the curse doesn't seem to have affected him. He's got a cart full of water which he's selling to the people here.

steps.speaker: Awusah the Mayor
steps.text: Unfortunately in typical Pollnivneach style he's taking the opportunity to sell the water at outrageous prices because he knows we are desperate. Oh and Rokuh has developed something quite remarkable, called a choc ice

steps.speaker: Awusah the Mayor
steps.text: which is helping people stay cool.

options.text: Any idea how you got this curse?

steps.player: Any idea how you got this curse?

steps.speaker: Awusah the Mayor
steps.text: Well we think it was because we were negligent in our duty to protect a priest of Saradomin. He came to us a few weeks ago from the north and we welcomed him into our town. He taught us much of the wisdom of

steps.speaker: Awusah the Mayor
steps.text: Saradomin. Then about a week ago, we found him dead by the river. It seems unlikely that it is coincidence we were then cursed. If you look around the town you might be able to find out more.

steps.prompt: Start the Spirits of the Elid quest?

options.text: Yes.

steps.player: Ok I will have a look around and see what I can do.

steps.speaker: Awusah the Mayor
steps.text: Good luck to you.

options.text: No.

steps.player: I'm sorry to hear of your plight, but I must be going.

options.text: I'm sorry to hear of your plight, but I must be going.

steps.player: I'm sorry to hear of your plight, but I must be going.

options.text: I'm just looking around.

steps.player: I'm just looking around.

steps.speaker: Awusah the Mayor
steps.text: Well we've not fallen on the best of times here, but there are a few shops to look around and we have someone selling a marvelous new invention called a choc ice..

steps.speaker: Awusah the Mayor
steps.text: Oh, and there's the old temple if you're interested in a bit of history.

options.text: I'm passing through on my way to Menaphos.

steps.player: I'm passing through on my way to Menaphos.

steps.speaker: Awusah the Mayor
steps.text: Oh you don't want to go there. I hear rumours of plagues and the like.

steps.player: Thanks for the warning, but I might go and investigate anyway.

starting-off-talking-to-awusah-after-sta.speaker: Awusah the Mayor
starting-off-talking-to-awusah-after-sta.text: Many salutations to you sir, have you made any progress in uncovering the reasons for our curse yet?

options.text: I am working on it.

steps.player: I am working on it.

steps.speaker: Awusah the Mayor
steps.text: Please try your best, that water salesman is not doing much good for the economy of our town.

options.text: What was I meant to do again?

steps.player: What was I meant to do again?

steps.speaker: Awusah the Mayor
steps.text: Look around this town, see if you can uncover any information to why we were cursed and how the curse might be lifted. I suspect that it might be because a priest of Saradomin died while staying at our town, but

steps.speaker: Awusah the Mayor
steps.text: that isn't much help in getting the curse lifted and it is possible I'm wrong anyway.

options.text: I haven't really had the time to investigate.

steps.player: I haven't really had the time to investigate.

steps.speaker: Awusah the Mayor
steps.text: Well I hope somebody can find the time soon, the despair of the people of this town increases daily.

starting-off-talking-to-ghaslor-the-elde.speaker: Ghaslor the Elder
starting-off-talking-to-ghaslor-the-elde.text: Good day to you young man.

options.text: I am trying to find out the cause of this town's curse.

steps.player: I am trying to find out the cause of this town's curse.

steps.speaker: Ghaslor the Elder
steps.text: Oh that's something which no one but the gods and the river spirits seem to know.

options.text: River spirits, what are they?

steps.player: River spirits, what are they?

steps.speaker: Ghaslor the Elder
steps.text: They're the guardians of the source of the river Elid, they'll know of our curse, seeing as it's related to water we bring from the river. It's said that nothing happens on the river that they don't know about.

steps.player: So would it be possible for me to find these spirits and ask them what is going on?

steps.speaker: Ghaslor the Elder
steps.text: Ahh now the spirits are something which no one from here have seen in a good long time, certainly not in my lifetime, I don't think even in my own grandfather's lifetime.

steps.speaker: Ghaslor the Elder
steps.text: Most the younger people of this town don't even remember that the spirits even exist.

steps.speaker: Ghaslor the Elder
steps.text: Here I have something around here somewhere which may be of interest to you.

steps.speaker: Ghaslor the Elder
steps.text: Aha yes here it is, the ballad of Jareesh. This tells of a previous quest to try and find the spirits.
Ghaslor hands you a scroll.

steps.player: Thank you very much for your help.

options.text: Thanks for your help.

steps.player: Thanks for your help.

options.text: How are things?

steps.player: How are things?

steps.speaker: Ghaslor the Elder
steps.text: Lousy, young people have no respect for their elders, there's too many confusing newfangled magic carpets and snake charmers around these days and now we don't even have any water.

steps.player: Well I hope things pick up for you.

options.text: I am trying to find out the cause of this town's curse.

steps.player: I am trying to find out the cause of this town's curse.

steps.speaker: Shiratti the Custodian
steps.text: Well with the moral standards of this town lately, I'm hardly surprised.

steps.player: Why, what have they been up to?

steps.speaker: Shiratti the Custodian
steps.text: Nothing someone like you would understand.

options.text: Good day to you.

steps.player: Good day to you.

steps.speaker: Shiratti the Custodian
steps.text: Be Careful in here and don't touch anything! There's some old and valuable artefacts around here. Careless outsiders.. you're always coming in and making a mess of things!

steps.player: Ok calm down, I'm not going to touch anything.

steps.speaker: Shiratti the Custodian
steps.text: Yes, good don't.

options.text: What is this building?

steps.player: What is this building?

steps.speaker: Shiratti the Custodian
steps.text: This is our local shrine to She.

steps.player: What do you mean by She?

steps.speaker: Shiratti the Custodian
steps.text: Such ignorance! I suppose I should come to expect it. People are forgetting the old ways of the desert around here. But then.. What do those bureaucratic fools in Menaphos expect! If they're going to take so long to

steps.speaker: Shiratti the Custodian
steps.text: send us a new priestess of She. Do you know we haven't had one for five years now!

steps.player: Errm you still haven't told me what you mean by She.

steps.speaker: Shiratti the Custodian
steps.text: She! Otherwise know as Elidinis, Goddess of growth and fertility, Lady of the river, Wife of Tumeken, Flower of the desert, Mother of Icthlarin.

steps.player: That all sounds very confusing, I might just call her Elidinis for short.

options.text: What is that key on display?

steps.player: What is that key on display?

steps.speaker: Shiratti the Custodian
steps.text: That's a very valuable artefact. Keep your hands off it.

steps.player: ..I just wanted to know what it did.

steps.speaker: Shiratti the Custodian
steps.text: That's the key to the holy chambers of the great and mighty Spirits of the Elid, and it's staying right there. There are other holy items about this building and keep your hands off them too, but most definitely keep your

steps.speaker: Shiratti the Custodian
steps.text: hands off the key. People already meddle too much with the affairs of the shrine.

starting-off-searching-the-north-western.text: You find a torn robe top.
You find some torn robe bottoms.

asking-around-the-town-ali-the-carter.speaker: Ali the Carter
asking-around-the-town-ali-the-carter.text: Water, water get your fresh water here, 1000 coins a waterskin, a bargain in these difficult times.

options.text: That's extortionate! Why so much?

steps.player: That's extortionate! Why so much?

steps.speaker: Ali the Carter
steps.text: Well it's the cheapest water you'll find in this town.

steps.player: Would you happen to know anything about the curse?

steps.speaker: Ali the Carter
steps.text: Yes the people round here can't seem to get the water themselves. It's an ideal business opportunity for one such as myself.

steps.player: It does seem to be slightly exploiting their unfortunate situation.

steps.speaker: Ali the Carter
steps.text: I don't see it like that. Without me they'd be in even more of a mess. I'm doing them a favour and in true Pollnivneachian spirit making a profit along the way.

options.text: Ok, I'll buy some!
I think I'll give it a miss.

asking-around-the-town-rokuh.speaker: Rokuh
asking-around-the-town-rokuh.text: Come one, come all, buy my amazing choc ice invention here! Chocolate on the outside. Iced cream on the inside. Oh I also have some chocolate left over from making choc ices which I'm selling too.

options.text: Cool I'd like to buy some.
No thanks, I'm not interested.
How do you stop your icy snacks melting?
I am trying to find out the cause of this town's curse.

steps.player: I am trying to find out the cause of this town's curse.

steps.speaker: Rokuh
steps.text: I really have no idea. It's most regrettable. Fortunately my innovation with my choc ice invention is helping people stay at least slightly cool.

asking-around-the-town-garai.player: Hi, I am trying to find the cause of the curse on your town.
Don't you know? The curse that has stopped your fountain working and made all the water dry up when you bring it back from the river?

asking-around-the-town-garai.speaker: Garai
asking-around-the-town-garai.text: Ohh that's because of a curse? I didn't think of that.

asking-around-the-town-garai.player: So any ideas about the cause of the curse?

asking-around-the-town-nkuku.player: Hi, I am trying to find the cause of the curse on your town.

asking-around-the-town-nkuku.speaker: Nkuku
asking-around-the-town-nkuku.text: It's terrible isn't it. Surely it is because we let the holy Saradominist priest die.

asking-around-the-town-usi.player: Hi, I am trying to find the cause of the curse on your town.

asking-around-the-town-usi.speaker: Usi
asking-around-the-town-usi.text: Well I think that's what everyone wants to know.

asking-around-the-town-habibah-meskhenet.player: Hi, I am trying to find the cause of the curse on your town.

asking-around-the-town-habibah-meskhenet.speaker: Habibah/Meskhenet/Zahra
asking-around-the-town-habibah-meskhenet.text: Ah I see. Awusah has enlisted your help?

asking-around-the-town-habibah-meskhenet.speaker: Habibah/Meskhenet/Zahra
asking-around-the-town-habibah-meskhenet.text: Well, I really don't know why it might have happened. Maybe Ghaslor has some ideas. He's very wise and old and is the town's archivist. He lives in the northeast corner of town.

asking-around-the-town-habibah-meskhenet.player: I heard the people of Nardah threw their statue of Elidinis away.

asking-around-the-town-habibah-meskhenet.speaker: Habibah/Meskhenet/Zahra
asking-around-the-town-habibah-meskhenet.text: Yes that's correct. Why do you ask?

asking-around-the-town-habibah-meskhenet.player: I've found out that action seems to have caused this town's curse.

asking-around-the-town-habibah-meskhenet.speaker: Habibah/Meskhenet/Zahra
asking-around-the-town-habibah-meskhenet.text: Well, I guess that would be logical conclusion. I don't really know where the statue was thrown. Awusah might know.

the-waterfall-attempting-to-open-the-doo.text: The ancestral key seems to fit the lock perfectly, but for some reason the doors still won't open.

the-waterfall-attempting-to-open-the-doo.player: That's odd. I wonder what I can have forgotten.

the-waterfall-opening-the-door-with-the-.text: You use your ancestral key to unlock the doors.

the-waterfall-guardian-golem-after-defea.text: The Golem disappears, but will be back to defend his door.

the-waterfall-talking-to-the-spirits-of-.speaker: Nirrie
the-waterfall-talking-to-the-spirits-of-.text: What brings thee to our domain? It has been a long time since

the-waterfall-talking-to-the-spirits-of-.speaker: Tirrie
the-waterfall-talking-to-the-spirits-of-.text: we have seen any of your kind. Thou art not even

options.text: Wow how do you finish each others sentences like that?

steps.player: Wow how do you finish each others sentences like that?

steps.speaker: Nirrie
steps.text: We are a gestalt entity. We each have our own body, but our minds

steps.speaker: Tirrie
steps.text: are united and we all think as one. Well except when Hallak doth leaveth

steps.speaker: Nirrie
steps.text: the toilet seat up.

steps.speaker: Hallak
steps.text: That's the way it's meant to be!

steps.speaker: Nirrie
steps.text: Ok we're a mostly gestalt entity. We each have own body, but

steps.speaker: Hallak
steps.text: our minds are united, except for some little parts which aren't. We mostly

steps.speaker: Tirrie
steps.text: think as one.

steps.player: That doesn't really have the same ring to it.

options.text: Give Nardah its water back!

steps.player: Give Nardah its water back!

steps.speaker: Nirrie
steps.text: This little one doth come blundering into our abode making demands, with no thought for

steps.speaker: Tirrie
steps.text: diplomacy or decorum.

options.text: I come as an emissary from the people of Nardah
Who are you calling little?

steps.player: Who are you calling little?

steps.speaker: Nirrie
steps.text: You are little in power compared to us.

options.text: Just tell me what it takes to get Nardah some water.

steps.player: Just tell me what it takes to get Nardah some water.

steps.speaker: Tirrie
steps.text: Thou shouldst calm down, getting worked up like that will not help thee.

options.text: I come as an emissary from the people of Nardah
Tell me what I need and I'll leave.

steps.player: Tell me what I need and I'll leave.

steps.speaker: Tirrie
steps.text: Well maybe we're not that desperate for thee to leave.

options.text: I come as an emissary from the people of Nardah
Look you don't want me to get annoyed.

steps.player: Look you don't want me to get annoyed.

steps.speaker: Nirrie
steps.text: That's a shame because thou art annoyed already.

options.text: I come as an emissary from the people of Nardah
Oh yes I'm annoyed, now give them their water.

steps.player: Oh yes I'm annoyed, now give them their water.

steps.speaker: Nirrie
steps.text: You know thou art really not skilled at diplomacy.

options.text: I come as an emissary from the people of Nardah
I haven't time for this nonsense.
I haven't time for this nonsense.
I haven't time for this nonsense.
I haven't time for this nonsense.

steps.player: I haven't time for this nonsense.

steps.speaker: Nirrie
steps.text: Well we know ye mortals are always in a rush with

steps.speaker: Tirrie
steps.text: your very busy little lives. We'd better let thee get on. We

steps.speaker: Hallak
steps.text: enjoyed thy visit.

options.text: Yes, it wasn't so easy getting in here.

steps.player: Yes, it wasn't so easy getting in here. Why have you made it so tough? You must really not like guests.

steps.speaker: Nirrie
steps.text: We are powerful spirits with direct contact to the great goddess Elidinis, we do not need to be bothered by the trifles of

steps.speaker: Tirrie
steps.text: each and every human. This way only those of much resource and intellect, may gain audience with us.

options.text: I come as an emissary from the people of Nardah.

steps.player: I come as an emissary from the people of Nardah. Their fountain has dried up and water they bring from the river dries up. What advice can you give on this matter?

steps.speaker: Nirrie
steps.text: How unusual, that the one who would come unto us on this issue isn't even from Nardah. Yes, it was indeed we

steps.speaker: Hallak
steps.text: who have withheld their water from them.

steps.player: Was this due to the death of the Saradominist priest as the towns people think?

steps.speaker: Nirrie
steps.text: No that also was our doing!

steps.speaker: Hallak
steps.text: He did not respect our ways and the ways of the desert! He did not respect the ways of Elidinis!

steps.speaker: Nirrie
steps.text: He came preaching the ways of Saradomin. Which is all well and good, but he also did turneth them from the path of the desert gods, especially Elidinis. Elidinis is happy to share the worship of followers, indeed Elidinis

steps.speaker: Nirrie
steps.text: was allied with Saradomin many ages past. Saradominist mages even gave us those golems you met as a diplomatic gesture, so you can see we have been on good terms. However this is an outrage.

options.text: Is there anything they can do to get their fountain working again?
Hey you've stopped finishing each others sentences.

steps.player: Hey you've stopped finishing each others sentences!

steps.speaker: Nirrie
steps.text: That seems to be something which happens when we get emotional

steps.speaker: Hallak
steps.text: We are

steps.speaker: Tirrie
steps.text: calmer now though.

options.text: Don't many other towns not follow Elidinis though?

steps.player: Don't many other towns not follow Elidinis though? Why pick on Nardah specifically?

steps.speaker: Tirrie
steps.text: This is the truth, but there is more to the story than that. The answers

steps.speaker: Hallak
steps.text: lie in the story of Nardarine. Wouldst thou likest to hear the telling of this tale? It is not a short one.

options.text: Yes I would like to hear this story.

steps.player: Yes I would like to hear this story.

steps.speaker: Tirrie
steps.text: Nardarine came from a town towards the north side of the desert which does not exist today. This was in the third age in the time thou callest

steps.speaker: Hallak
steps.text: the God Wars. Her town was once controlled by Saradomin, but there was a great battle there between Saradominist and Zamorakian forces which pretty much levelled the town

steps.speaker: Nirrie
steps.text: to the ground. Most of the human citizens perished. Nardarine had the wisdom to escape into the desert before the fighting got really serious and thus survived. However she found herself wandering lost and alone in

steps.speaker: Tirrie
steps.text: the desert. She prayed to Saradomin for help, but Saradomin was too concerned with the loss of a strategic outpost to worry about the fate of one small human. Nardarine had wandered towards the realm of

steps.speaker: Hallak
steps.text: the Menaphite God Pantheon. Elidinis heard the prayers of Nardarine, she took pity on the wandering human and came unto her with water. 'Oh great goddess' exclaimed Nardarine 'I wish not to be involved more in

steps.speaker: Nirrie
steps.text: the wars of the gods for they have caused me so much hardship already, I wish only for a quiet life somewhere'. Elidinis replied 'I will grant this unto thee on the condition that thou swearest to forever pay fealty and

steps.speaker: Tirrie
steps.text: homage to me and I grant this also unto thine descendents as long as they too will pay an oath of fealty and homage to me'. Nardarine said 'If you would grant me a safe home, with a

steps.speaker: Hallak
steps.text: supply of food and water, then I would surely do this for it is more than any other God would seem to do for me'. Then Elidinis made

steps.speaker: Nirrie
steps.text: a spring of water appear at Nardarines feet and brought stone from below the sand so that she

steps.speaker: Tirrie
steps.text: might have something to build with. She called forth camels which have many uses and taste good in kebabs. She then provided Nardarine with a statuette in her image to worship. Nardarine built up her home. Over

steps.speaker: Hallak
steps.text: time more refugees from the God Wars found Nardarine's home. Nardarine let them stay with her as long as they did make the same oath as her. Hence the town of Nardah was born and Nardarine lived the rest

steps.speaker: Nirrie
steps.text: of her days in the peacefulness that she craved. The oath was passed down the generations for many ages, but now seemeth to be forgotten. Now maybe thou canst see why we are not best pleased.

steps.player: That does make some sense.
Is there anything they can do to get their fountain working again?

steps.speaker: Nirrie
steps.text: I do not know. The Saradominist priest persuaded the people of Nardah to throw away a statuette of Elidinis which was in the temple. As long as they do not have that image of Elidinis to pray to, then we must consider

steps.speaker: Nirrie
steps.text: them turned away from her and the curse shalt stand.

steps.player: Well that's all very interesting, I wonder what the people of Nardah will think of this.

options.text: Is there anything they can do to get their fountain working again?
What manner of beings are you?

steps.player: What manner of beings are you?

steps.speaker: Nirrie
steps.text: We are the spirits of the river Elid, many ages ago we used to be mindless wandering spirits, with little mind or purpose, we were here even in the first age. Then great Elidinis came to the desert and bound us to her

steps.speaker: Nirrie
steps.text: river, we've

steps.speaker: Tirrie
steps.text: become one with the river and over the centuries become full of the power of Elidinis that was in her river. We are now her trusted guardians of the Elid, we can control the river and anything which happens

steps.speaker: Tirrie
steps.text: near the river we know about.

steps.player: Tell me more of Elidinis.

steps.speaker: Nirrie
steps.text: Elidinis is one of a group of gods, known as the Menaphite Pantheon. She is the wife of their leader Tumeken. She is the Menaphite goddess of growth and fertility, and goddess of the river.

options.text: Wow how do you finish each others sentences like that?
Give Nardah its water back!
I come as an emissary from the people of Nardah.
Give Nardah its water back!

steps.player: Give Nardah its water back!

steps.speaker: Hallak
steps.text: I thought we had been through this already. You are not in any position to make such demands. As long as they do not have their statuette of Elidinis to pray to, then we

steps.speaker: Tirrie
steps.text: must consider them turned away from her and the curse shalt stand.

options.text: Yes, it's nice and cool here.

steps.player: Yes, it's nice and cool here.

steps.speaker: Hallak
steps.text: That it is, praise the power of Elidinis.

options.text: What did the townspeople need to do again?

steps.text: As long as they do not have their statuette of Elidinis to pray to, then we

the-crevice-talking-to-awusah-the-mayor.speaker: Awusah the Mayor
the-crevice-talking-to-awusah-the-mayor.text: Many salutations to you sir, have you made any progress in uncovering the reasons for our curse yet?

the-crevice-talking-to-awusah-the-mayor.player: Yes I have made some progress. It is the doing of the water spirits at the source of the river.

the-crevice-talking-to-awusah-the-mayor.speaker: Awusah the Mayor
the-crevice-talking-to-awusah-the-mayor.text: The Spirits of the Elid? I wasn't even sure if they weren't some old wives tale. Why would they do such a thing?

the-crevice-talking-to-awusah-the-mayor.player: Did you by any chance throw away a statuette of the goddess Elidinis recently?

the-crevice-talking-to-awusah-the-mayor.speaker: Awusah the Mayor
the-crevice-talking-to-awusah-the-mayor.text: Oh that old thing. Yeah, the priest of Saradomin said we should get rid of that. He said we should become followers of Saradomin, and therefore we wouldn't need it.

the-crevice-talking-to-awusah-the-mayor.player: Well the spirits killed him for imparting that piece of advice about the statuette.
Apparently this town was brought about by Elidinis on the promise that its people would follow her. People here have been waning in their belief of Elidinis for a while now.
It seems the casting away of the statue was the final straw.

the-crevice-talking-to-awusah-the-mayor.speaker: Awusah the Mayor
the-crevice-talking-to-awusah-the-mayor.text: Ohh that's not so good if only we hadn't thrown the statue away, we wouldn't have this water problem then. He was a very convincing priest though. He worked many wonders, for example if he prayed hard enough

the-crevice-talking-to-awusah-the-mayor.speaker: Awusah the Mayor
the-crevice-talking-to-awusah-the-mayor.text: he became impervious to arrows. The way of Saradomin did seem very appealing.

steps.speaker: Awusah the Mayor
steps.text: Then truly you are very powerful too!

the-crevice-talking-to-awusah-the-mayor.player: Where did you throw the statuette?

the-crevice-talking-to-awusah-the-mayor.speaker: Awusah the Mayor
the-crevice-talking-to-awusah-the-mayor.text: Ohh there's a strange deep crevice in the desert to the west of here. We threw it down there. I don't know if it's lost forever or not.

the-crevice-talking-to-awusah-the-mayor.player: Well it's worth a look anyway.

the-crevice-talking-to-awusah-the-mayor.speaker: Awusah the Mayor
the-crevice-talking-to-awusah-the-mayor.text: If you could retrieve it for us we'll be very grateful. Even if it doesn't give us our water back, maybe it'll calm Shiratti down, she was not pleased at it being thrown away and she's been grumpy ever since.

the-crevice-talking-to-awusah-the-mayor-.speaker: Awusah the Mayor
the-crevice-talking-to-awusah-the-mayor-.text: Have you had any luck retrieving our statuette yet?

options.text: Not yet, but don't give up hope yet.

steps.player: Not yet, but don't give up hope yet.

steps.speaker: Awusah the Mayor
steps.text: Good luck, may Sarad.. errm I mean Elidinis guide you.

options.text: Where did you say you threw it again?

steps.player: Where did you say you threw it again?

steps.speaker: Awusah the Mayor
steps.text: In a deep crevice to the west of this village.

the-crevice-talking-to-shiratti-the-cust.player: I'm told that a statuette was removed from this temple.

the-crevice-talking-to-shiratti-the-cust.speaker: Shiratti the Custodian
the-crevice-talking-to-shiratti-the-cust.text: Yes, that Saradominist priest brought a group of the villagers in here. Took it by force as far as I'm concerned. I'm not at all happy, standards have been slipping here for a while, but that was going too far.

the-crevice-talking-to-shiratti-the-cust.speaker: Shiratti the Custodian
the-crevice-talking-to-shiratti-the-cust.text: She! Elidinis! Goddess of growth and fertility! Lady of the River, Wife of Tumeken, Flower of the Desert. Mother of Icthlarin!

the-crevice-talking-to-shiratti-the-cust.player: ..Ah yes, that She. Well you're right, that would be an insult to Elidinis. In fact it seems that affront is what has brought the curse upon this village.

the-crevice-talking-to-shiratti-the-cust.speaker: Shiratti the Custodian
the-crevice-talking-to-shiratti-the-cust.text: Well you know I suspected that all along, but does anyone listen to me anymore? No! Well I'm impressed you've come to the same conclusion as me, maybe I underestimated you.

the-crevice-talking-to-shiratti-the-cust.player: Er, why didn't you tell me about your suspicions when I was asking around about the curse then?

the-crevice-talking-to-shiratti-the-cust.speaker: Shiratti the Custodian
the-crevice-talking-to-shiratti-the-cust.text: I have to apologise. We've already had one outsider around stirring trouble, which caused this whole mess in the first place. I feared that you were coming to force your ways on us.

the-crevice-talking-to-shiratti-the-cust.speaker: Shiratti the Custodian
the-crevice-talking-to-shiratti-the-cust.text: Well I'm grateful, anything you can do to find the statuette would be appreciated.

the-crevice-talking-to-ghaslor-the-elder.speaker: Ghaslor the Elder
the-crevice-talking-to-ghaslor-the-elder.text: Good day to you young man.

the-crevice-talking-to-ghaslor-the-elder.speaker: Ghaslor the Elder
the-crevice-talking-to-ghaslor-the-elder.text: Any progress on uncovering the town's curse yet?

the-crevice-talking-to-ghaslor-the-elder.player: Yes some actually. I managed to speak to the river spirits you told me about.

the-crevice-talking-to-ghaslor-the-elder.speaker: Ghaslor the Elder
the-crevice-talking-to-ghaslor-the-elder.text: You actually managed to find them? I'm impressed. As I say - no one has seen them in many many years.

the-crevice-talking-to-ghaslor-the-elder.player: Yes the spirits told me that the town is cursed because you guys have thrown away a statuette to the goddess Elidinis.

the-crevice-talking-to-ghaslor-the-elder.speaker: Ghaslor the Elder
the-crevice-talking-to-ghaslor-the-elder.text: Ah yes I heard a group led by that Saradominist priest went into the shrine and removed the Statuette. It all seemed a bit unnecessary to me. Didn't realise it would curse us though.

the-crevice-talking-to-ghaslor-the-elder.speaker: Ghaslor the Elder
the-crevice-talking-to-ghaslor-the-elder.text: I have no idea what they did with it afterwards.

the-crevice-talking-to-the-genie.speaker: Genie
the-crevice-talking-to-the-genie.text: I am a mighty and powerful genie. Why do you come here? Speak now or I'll have to think of something exceedingly nasty to do to you.

options.text: You're a genie, grant me a wish.

steps.player: You're a genie, grant me a wish.

steps.speaker: Genie
steps.text: Not all genies are goody two shoes who go round granting wishes. It's something that my pathetic brother does to make people like him, but that's not my style.

steps.speaker: Genie
steps.text: I like to think of myself more as an evil and scary sort of genie, who people talk about in hushed and fearful tones.

options.text: Well you seem quite scary.

steps.player: Well you seem quite scary.

steps.speaker: Genie
steps.text: Why thank you, I put a lot of effort into my terrifyingness.

steps.speaker: Genie
steps.text: Wait! Did you say quite scary? I'll have you know I am VERY scary!

steps.player: Erm yes that's what I meant.

options.text: I'm after a statue that was thrown down here.
Why are you sitting here in the dark.
Well I must be off now.

steps.player: Well I must be off now.

steps.speaker: Genie
steps.text: Yes, run. Ruuuun in fear of.. The crevice genie of Nardah! Muhahaha!

options.text: Why are you sitting here in the dark?

steps.player: Why are you sitting here in the dark?

steps.speaker: Genie
steps.text: Two reasons really. Firstly, I can see in the dark, so light or dark makes little difference to me.

steps.speaker: Genie
steps.text: Lastly, I gather it's normal for powerful terrifying creatures to lurk around in dark caves, so I found this one to lurk in myself, nice isn't it?

options.text: Very pleasant, the snakes are a nice touch.

steps.player: Very pleasant, the snakes are a nice touch.

steps.speaker: Genie
steps.text: Why do I get the sense that I'm not being taken seriously here? Please try to remember I am very dangerous and not to be trifled with.

options.text: I'm after a statue that was thrown down here.
You're a genie, grant me a wish.
Well I must be off now.
I'm just looking around.

steps.player: I'm just looking around.

steps.speaker: Genie
steps.text: I don't know about that. I can't have just anybody traipsing in here. I have a reputation to keep you see.

steps.speaker: Genie
steps.text: Actually I'll tell you what, you can hang around here for a bit, but be sure to spread the word about what a terrifying experience you had when you ran into... The crevice genie of Nardah!

steps.player: ...Ok I think I can manage that.

the-crevice-talking-to-the-genie-again-a.speaker: Genie
the-crevice-talking-to-the-genie-again-a.text: Do you have the sole of Awusah, so that we can make our trade?

options.text: How am I meant to remove someone's soul?
I'm still working on it.

steps.player: I'm still working on it.

steps.speaker: Genie
steps.text: Well no rush, I quite like the statuette too.

options.text: No, it's not an easy thing to get.

steps.player: No, it's not an easy thing to get.

steps.speaker: Genie
steps.text: Haha, even a pathetic human should be able to manage to get another human's sole.

sole-split-talking-to-the-mayor-again.speaker: Awusah the Mayor
sole-split-talking-to-the-mayor-again.text: Have you had any luck retrieving our statuette yet?

sole-split-talking-to-the-mayor-again.player: Err, well I have made some progress. I met a genie down the crevice. He told me that he would give me the statuette in exchange for your soul.

sole-split-talking-to-the-mayor-again.speaker: Awusah the Mayor
sole-split-talking-to-the-mayor-again.text: What! That's just asking to much. So, he want's to have my soul when my time to die comes?

sole-split-talking-to-the-mayor-again.player: Well not exactly, he sort of basically said I should remove it with a knife.

sole-split-talking-to-the-mayor-again.speaker: Awusah the Mayor
sole-split-talking-to-the-mayor-again.text: That's barbaric! I simply refuse. The price is too high. We'll just have to find other ways to get the town a good supply of water. Don't go bringing any knives near me.

sole-split-using-a-knife-on-awusah-the-m.speaker: Awusah the Mayor
sole-split-using-a-knife-on-awusah-the-m.text: What do you think you are doing?

sole-split-using-a-knife-on-awusah-the-m.player: Errm, I'm trying to remove your soul.

sole-split-using-a-knife-on-awusah-the-m.speaker: Awusah the Mayor
sole-split-using-a-knife-on-awusah-the-m.text: What, have you lost your mind?

sole-split-using-a-knife-on-awusah-the-m.player: It's for the good of the village. I met a genie down the crevice. He told me that he would give me the statuette in exchange for your sole.

sole-split-using-a-knife-on-awusah-the-m.speaker: Awusah the Mayor
sole-split-using-a-knife-on-awusah-the-m.text: That's barbaric! We'll just have to find other ways to get the town a good supply of water. Keep your knife away from me please.

sole-split-cutting-the-mayor-s-shoes.text: You remove the soles from the shoes.

sole-split-returning-to-the-genie-with-t.speaker: Genie
sole-split-returning-to-the-genie-with-t.text: Do you have the sole of Awusah, so that we can make our trade?

sole-split-returning-to-the-genie-with-t.speaker: Genie
sole-split-returning-to-the-genie-with-t.text: Ah excellent, here's the statuette then.
You trade the sole for the statuette.

sole-split-returning-to-the-genie-with-t.player: So um, why do you need part of Awusah's footwear anyway? I hope you're not going to do some nasty magic on his feet or something.

sole-split-returning-to-the-genie-with-t.speaker: Genie
sole-split-returning-to-the-genie-with-t.text: I hadn't thought of that. I just read that a lot of the most powerful beings are collecting soles these days. I haven't really got many yet though. You provided me with an opportunity to expand my collection.

sole-split-talking-to-the-genie-after-lo.speaker: Genie
sole-split-talking-to-the-genie-after-lo.text: Well fortunately for you, I am a mighty and powerful genie and managed to reacquire it. I will give it to you for another sole.
If the player has a sole:

steps.player: Yes I have one here.

steps.speaker: Genie
steps.text: Ah excellent here's the statuette then.
You trade the sole for the statuette.

steps.speaker: Genie
steps.text: It's good doing business with you again.

sole-split-talking-to-the-genie-after-lo.text: If the player does not have a sole:

steps.player: I will go and get one then.

steps.speaker: Genie
steps.text: Great! Another one for my collection.

sole-split-talking-to-the-mayor-with-the.speaker: Awusah the Mayor
sole-split-talking-to-the-mayor-with-the.text: Have you had any luck retrieving our statuette yet?

sole-split-talking-to-the-mayor-with-the.player: Yes I finally got it. I had to destroy a pair of your shoes though. A crazy genie wanted a sole off your shoe in return for the statuette. I think he got souls and soles confused.

sole-split-talking-to-the-mayor-with-the.speaker: Awusah the Mayor
sole-split-talking-to-the-mayor-with-the.text: I suppose sacrificing a pair of shoes for the greater good of the town is reasonable. I don't begin to understand the ways of genies.

sole-split-talking-to-the-mayor-with-the.player: Yes I thought it best not to correct him. He's somewhat less dangerous than he might be if he's a collector of shoe soles.

sole-split-talking-to-the-mayor-with-the.speaker: Awusah the Mayor
sole-split-talking-to-the-mayor-with-the.text: Anyway thanks for getting the statue back. You should take it to our temple and then we can see if our fountain starts working again.

sole-split-talking-to-shiratti-with-the-.speaker: Shiratti the Custodian
sole-split-talking-to-shiratti-with-the-.text: That is great news! I could kiss you, but they don't allow shrine custodians to engage in that sort of behaviour. You should put the statuette back on its plinth.
